To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the arsenic concentrations in the ground water are high and the most probable mechanism of arsenic mobilization is reductive dissolution of iron hydroxides.

the arsenic concentration in the ground water of Ballia district was mainly controlled by the reduction of FeOOH and that the concentration of As (III) in the ground water was generally equal or higher than As(V).
the arsenic concentration is not much affected by seasonal variation and the reductive dissolution of iron oxyhydroxides is the main process of arsenic release into ground water.
In summary, our research is concerned with
arsenic geochemistry of ground water of Ballia district of Uttar Pradesh, India.
the geochemical characteristics of ground water arsenics in Ballia district.
the geochemistry of ground water and arsenic in Ballia district, UP, India and the possible processes controlling the release of arsenic into ground water.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the geochemical processes responsible for arsenic release in Ballia are similar to those reported for other parts of West Bengal and Bangladesh, but the magnitude of arsenic contamination in Ballia is much lower.

arsenic in the study area is released from the aquifer matrix by reductive dissolution of iron oxides and is transported by the reducing conditions in the shallow aquifer and is not a recent phenomenon as the concentration of As in deep aquifer (66-75m) is lower than that of the shallow aquifer (30-33m).
arsenic is released into ground water from iron oxide minerals by reduction of iron oxides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the geochemical conditions in the study area are not suitable for the mobilization of arsenic into ground water.
the Ballia district of Uttar Pradesh has a high risk of arsenic contamination in its ground waters.
the arsenic contamination in ground water in Ballia district is due to the reductive dissolution of iron hydroxides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the arsenic concentrations are not only high, but the spatial variability is very high.
arsenic is mobilized from the aquifer by reductive dissolution of iron oxyhydroxides, and this mechanism is more effective in shallow aquifers.
